propositions.text: The Appellant is a Turkish citizen appealing the RPD's denial of refugee protection.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX (the "Appellant") is a citizen of Turkey and is appealing a decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) denying his claim for refugee protection.

propositions.text: The RPD erred in assessing the objective basis for risk upon return to Turkey.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that the RPD erred in its assessment of the objective basis for his risk upon return to Turkey.

propositions.text: The RPD failed to consider key documentation about similarly-situated persons and forward-looking risk of perceived support for the XXXX movement.
propositions.quote: the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) finds that the RPD failed to consider key documentation regarding similarly-situated persons and failed to consider the Appellant's forward-looking risk on the basis that he would be perceived to be a supporter of the XXXX movement if he returned to Turkey.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Appellant is a Turkish citizen appealing the RPD's denial, arguing RPD erred in risk assessment; the court finds RPD failed to consider key evidence.

propositions.text: The appeal is allowed and the Appellant is found to be a Convention refugee.
propositions.quote: For the reasons provided below, I allow the appeal and find the Appellant is a Convention refugee.

paragraphs.summary: The court allows the appeal and finds the Appellant is a Convention refugee.

propositions.text: The Appellant joined Turkish Armed Forces in 2012 and was a cadet at the Military Academy.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleges that he joined the Turkish Armed Forces in XXXX 2012 and that he was a XXXX XXXX at the Turkish Military Academy.

propositions.text: After the 2016 coup attempt, government purged cadets perceived involved, including torture and arrests.
propositions.quote: After the attempted coup in Turkey on July 15, 2016, he alleges that the government started targeting and purging cadets from the military due to their perceived involvement in the attempted coup, for which he states he was not involved.

propositions.text: Many military people were arrested and tortured, including fellow cadets.
propositions.quote: The Appellant claims that many military people were arrested and tortured following the coup, including many of his fellow cadets.

propositions.text: He and other cadets were transferred to other universities; diploma blacklists him as involved in the coup.
propositions.quote: As a result of this purge, he and other cadets were transferred to other universities. Upon graduation, his university diploma noted that it was provided by XXXX University under the auspices of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, which he alleges effectively blacklists him as a member of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and for having been involved in the attempted coup.

propositions.text: He arrived in Canada in 2017 on a student visa and claimed refugee protection inland in May 2017.
propositions.quote: In XXXX 2017, he obtained a student visa and arrived in Canada in February 2017. The Appellant made an inland claim for refugee protection in May 2017.

propositions.text: He fears detention, arrest, torture, or unfair trial if returned due to perceived membership in XXXX.
propositions.quote: If he returns to Turkey, he fears detention, arrest, torture, and/or being subject to an unfair trial due to the perception that he is a member of XXXX.

propositions.text: Further details are in his Basis of Claim form and RPD hearing testimony.
propositions.quote: Further details are provided in his Basis of Claim (BOC) Form, and his testimony at the RPD hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant alleges joining Turkish Armed Forces in 2012, purged after 2016 coup, fears persecution if returned; arrived in Canada 2017 and claimed refugee protection.

propositions.text: The Appellant had a refugee hearing on July 26, 2017; RPD decision issued November 16, 2017 rejecting claim.
propositions.quote: The Appellant had a refugee determination hearing on July 26, 2017. In a written decision issued on November 16, 2017, the RPD rejected the claim.

propositions.text: RPD found no reasonable chance of persecution, only a chance, so no well-founded fear on Convention grounds.
propositions.quote: The RPD panel found the Appellant did not have an objective basis for his fear of persecution, as there is a chance of persecution, not a reasonable chance of persecution.

propositions.text: RPD concluded Appellant would not face risk to life, cruel treatment, or torture upon return.
propositions.quote: Therefore, the RPD concluded that the Appellant does not have a well-founded fear of persecution on a Convention ground, or that he would not personally be subjected to a risk to life or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or a danger of torture upon return to Turkey.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD held a hearing and rejected the claim, finding only a chance, not reasonable chance, of persecution or risk upon return.

propositions.text: RAD applies correctness standard for fact, mixed fact and law, and law questions per Huruglica.
propositions.quote: For questions of fact, mixed fact and law, and law, the RAD applies the standard of correctness in accordance with the Federal Court of Appeal's decision in Huruglica.

propositions.text: RAD may apply modified reasonableness for credibility findings where RPD has meaningful advantage.
propositions.quote: In assessing findings involving the credibility of oral testimony, the RAD may apply the modified standard of reasonableness in situations where the RPD enjoys a meaningful advantage.

propositions.text: RAD uses correctness standard on all findings unless otherwise stated, including overall refugee determination.
propositions.quote: Unless otherwise stated in the reasons, the RAD uses the correctness standard on all findings and will consider the overall refugee determination on a standard of correctness, even where the RAD has deferred on some or all findings.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD applies correctness standard generally, modified reasonableness for credibility where RPD has advantage, per Huruglica.

propositions.text: Evidence from appellant admissible on appeal only if it meets IRPA s.110(4) conditions: arose after, not reasonably available, or could not reasonably be presented earlier.
propositions.quote: Evidence from the person who is the subject of the appeal is only admissible on appeal if it meets one of the statutory conditions set out in subsection 110(4) of the IRPA, namely that it arose after, or was not reasonably available, or the person could not reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to have presented the evidence at the time the claim was rejected.

propositions.text: If conditions met, RAD considers if evidence is credible, relevant, and new per Singh.
propositions.quote: If one of these conditions is met, the RAD will then consider if the evidence is credible, relevant, and new as endorsed by the Federal Court of Appeal in Singh.

paragraphs.summary: The court states evidence admissible on appeal only if it meets IRPA s.110(4) and is credible, relevant, and new per Singh.

propositions.text: Appellant submits four documents as new evidence, all postdating RPD decision.
propositions.quote: the Appellant appears to submit four documents as new evidence, all of which postdate the RPD's decision rejecting his claim.

propositions.text: The four documents are three Memurlar.net articles and an updated National Documentation Package (NDP).
propositions.quote: 1) Memurlar.net, "XXXX operation in 49 cities: 240 people were taken into custody", dated 30 November 2017; 2) Memurlar.net, "16 of 20 suspects, who were taken into custody, were sent to prison", dated 25 December 2017; 3) Memurlar.net, "Operation against XXXX Private Military Structure", dated 17 January 2018; and, 4) National Documentation Package (NDP) for Turkey, dated 21 December 2017.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant submits four new documents postdating the RPD decision: three news articles and an updated NDP.

propositions.text: First three Memurlar.net documents accepted as new evidence as they postdate RPD decision and are credible and relevant.
propositions.quote: I accept the first three documents listed above as new evidence. They postdate the RPD's decision and describe events in Turkey since the Appellant's claim was rejected.

propositions.text: Documents are relevant to treatment of similarly-situated persons and credible with no reason to doubt source.
propositions.quote: In addition, the documents are "relevant" to describing the treatment of persons similarly-situated to the Appellant. They are also "credible" as I have no reason to doubt the source and circumstances in which this information was reported and came about.

propositions.text: Singh criteria met; Memurlar.net articles admitted as new evidence.
propositions.quote: For these reasons, I find the Singh criteria are met in this case and I admit the articles from Memurlar.net as new evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The court admits the first three Memurlar.net documents as new, credible, relevant evidence meeting Singh criteria.

propositions.text: Appellant relies on March 31, 2017 NDP version before RPD; no submissions on updated NDP relevance.
propositions.quote: the Appellant's own memorandum chooses to rely on the content of the NDP dated March 31, 2017, which was the version of the NDP before the RPD. The Appellant does not indicate what information in the updated NDP is new or relevant to the issues in this appeal.

propositions.text: Updated NDP not shown to be relevant or new; does not impact appeal disposition.
propositions.quote: I find the relevance and newness factor in Singh is not established. Furthermore, in my review of the updated NDP, nothing turns on the updated content, nor does it impact the disposition in this appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the updated NDP not shown to be relevant or new and it does not affect the appeal outcome.

propositions.text: Two recent RAD decisions provided are case law, not evidence, so not admitted as new evidence.
propositions.quote: I note that the Appellant provided two recent RAD decisions in his Appeal Record, which were decided since the Appellant's RPD decision. However, I will not consider this as new evidence, as this is appropriately considered case law relied upon in the Appellant's submissions. Case law is not evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The court will not consider recent RAD decisions as new evidence since case law is not evidence.

propositions.text: Appellant does not request oral hearing; new evidence does not raise serious credibility issues.
propositions.quote: The Appellant does not specifically request an oral hearing based on this new evidence. Although I have found documentary evidence admissible as new evidence, I find that the new evidence does not raise a serious issue with respect to the credibility of the person who is the subject of the appeal.

propositions.text: Oral hearing not necessary as criteria of s.110(6) not met.
propositions.quote: Therefore, the criteria of 110(6) is not met and an oral hearing is not necessary in this case.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no oral hearing necessary as the new evidence does not raise serious credibility issues and no request was made.

propositions.text: Whether the RPD erred in analyzing the Appellant's objective risk based on perceived involvement or support of XXXX movement.
propositions.quote: The determinative issue is whether the RPD erred in its analysis of the Appellant's objective risk on the basis of his perceived involvement in XXXX or as a supporter of the XXXX movement.

paragraphs.summary: The court identifies the key issue as whether the RPD erred in assessing the Appellant's objective risk due to perceived XXXX involvement.

propositions.text: RPD did not dispute underlying facts and should consider them credible.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that the underlying facts of his allegations were not disputed by the RPD and should be considered as credible.

propositions.text: RPD erroneously downplayed objective evidence, finding only a 'chance' not 'reasonable chance' of persecution.
propositions.quote: the Appellant argues that the RPD significantly and erroneously downplayed the objective documentary evidence about the risk to him if he returned to Turkey by finding there was a "chance", but not a "reasonable chance" of persecution if he returned to Turkey as a dismissed XXXX XXXX.

propositions.text: Government targeted military cadets believing XXXX infiltrated schools; Erdogan said 95% cadets are 'XXXX'.
propositions.quote: it is obvious from the record that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and the closure of the military schools was the government's response to its belief that XXXX had infiltrated the schools and that they were targeting military cadets. This is supported by President Erdogan's statement that he believes that 95% of the military cadets are "XXXX".

propositions.text: RPD wrongly concluded Appellant falls into 5% not perceived as affiliated with XXXX.
propositions.quote: Despite this, the RPD seems to conclude that the Appellant somehow falls into the 5% of cadets who are not perceived as being affiliated to XXXX.

propositions.text: No dispute that cadets are arrested and detained at accelerating rates; no basis for RPD's opposite conclusion.
propositions.quote: There is also no dispute that cadets in Turkey are arrested and detained at accelerating rates, and as such, there is no basis for the RPD's conclusion that the evidence demonstrates the opposite.

propositions.text: Appellant dismissed due to closure of military schools targeting XXXX affiliates.
propositions.quote: The evidence shows that the Appellant was dismissed from the military as a result of the closure of the military schools, an action taken by the Turkish government in response to its belief that XXXX had infiltrated these schools and the cadets were accordingly affiliated with XXXX.

propositions.text: Family members reported on suspicion of XXXX membership.
propositions.quote: He also notes that many of his family members including his aunt and cousin have been reported to the authorities on the suspicion of being members of the XXXX Movement.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues RPD did not dispute facts, downplayed evidence, wrongly concluded he was not perceived as XXXX, and family members were reported as XXXX suspects.

propositions.text: RPD's finding that Appellant could exit Turkey is contrary to case law; assessment must be forward-looking.
propositions.quote: With respect to the RPD's finding that he was able to exit Turkey, the Appellant argues that this finding is contrary to the case law, which states this is not determinative and that the assessment must be forward-looking.

propositions.text: Appellant not required to show he is wanted by authorities.
propositions.quote: He submits he is not required to show that he is wanted by the authorities.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence shows military cadets continue to be arrested for perceived XXXX involvement.
propositions.quote: On a forward-looking assessment, the Appellant states that the documentary evidence shows that military cadets continue to be arrested and detained for their perceived XXXX involvement.

propositions.text: RPD ignored evidence of similarly-situated individuals and news articles about treatment of former cadets.
propositions.quote: the Appellant argues that the RPD ignored evidence submitted in the record of similarly-situated individuals and additional news articles about the treatment of former military cadets in Turkey.

propositions.text: Includes positive RPD decision for Appellant's friend, a former XXXX XXXX, on same facts.
propositions.quote: This included a positive RPD decision of the Appellant's friend, which is based on the same facts as a former XXXX XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues RPD wrongly relied on his exit from Turkey, ignored evidence of ongoing arrests, and a positive decision for a similarly-situated friend.

propositions.text: The RPD erred by ignoring key documentary evidence including similarly-situated individuals.
propositions.quote: I agree with the Appellant's argument and find the RPD erred. The RPD ignored key evidence in the documentary evidence, including of similarly-situated individuals.

propositions.text: RPD did not dispute core facts: Appellant was a dismissed XXXX XXXX and diploma noted XXXX affiliation.
propositions.quote: In addition, I agree with the Appellant that the RPD did not dispute the underlying facts of the case, which were that the Appellant was a XXXX XXXX and dismissed following the attempted coup. It also did not dispute that his diploma indicated that it was awarded under the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, which was implemented shortly after the attempted coup.

propositions.text: Appellant credible in core allegations; key issue is forward-looking risk of persecution as dismissed XXXX XXXX.
propositions.quote: Based on my review of the record, I find the Appellant credible in these core allegations, and therefore, the determinative issue is whether the Appellant's profile as a dismissed XXXX XXXX places him at a forward-looking risk of persecution.

propositions.text: For reasons that follow, the claim is well-founded.
propositions.quote: For the reasons that follow, I find that his claim is well-founded.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD erred ignoring evidence, accepts core facts and credibility, and finds the claim well-founded on forward-looking risk.

propositions.text: Amnesty International reports anyone linked to XXXX accused of coup is targeted, including many professions.
propositions.quote: Amnesty International reports that "[a]nyone with any perceived link to the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX accused of orchestrating the coup, has been targeted. Soldiers, police, judges, lawyers, academics, journalists, teachers, doctors and even football referees. Seemingly, no one is immune."

propositions.text: NDP states Turkish government calls XXXX a terrorist organization and applies overbroad terrorism laws.
propositions.quote: Item 4.11 of the NDP says that the Turkish government has called XXXX (XXXX XXXX XXXX) a terrorist organization. The document goes on to say that Human Rights Watch notes that being labelled a terrorist group allows Turkey to apply "overbroad terrorism laws against suspected XXXX."

propositions.text: Government purge targets people based on perceived association with XXXX, with beatings and torture in detention.
propositions.quote: This document expressly states that the Turkish government's "purge" has gone too far beyond its scope and is now targeting people based on their perceived association with XXXX. Those who have been detained have been "subjected to beatings and torture, including rape, in official and unofficial detention centres in the country."

propositions.text: Trials criticized for lacking fair trial, due process, and legal remedies.
propositions.quote: Trials of those arrested and charged have been criticized as not preserving defendants' rights to a fair trial, due process and legal remedies.

paragraphs.summary: Amnesty International and NDP report Turkish government targets perceived XXXX associates with overbroad laws, torture, and unfair trials.

propositions.text: Rhetoric shows state intent to 'cleanse' Turkey of XXXX supporters, creating fear and risk of harm.
propositions.quote: The rhetoric towards XXXX supporters and sympathizers also indicates a clear intention of state authorities to "cleanse" Turkey of all of its elements, demonstrating an overall context of fear and risk of harm to those seen as XXXX supporters.

propositions.text: President Erdogan called XXXX supporters 'viruses' and urged citizens to report them to authorities.
propositions.quote: President Erdogan has called XXXX supporters "viruses" and called on Turkish citizens to report them to prosecutors and security agencies, even if they are your friends.

propositions.text: Turkish citizens encouraged to inform on neighbors; even diaspora pressured to report XXXX sympathizers abroad.
propositions.quote: The Turkish President has called on Turks to inform on their fellow citizens, and so the whispered word of a neighbour with a grudge could be enough to land someone in jail. This initiative is not limited to within Turkey's borders, as the European Commission reports that members of the Turkish diaspora are under pressure to report to Turkish authorities XXXX sympathizers they know who reside in their communities abroad, and that Erdogan threatens that no region in the world is a safe haven for XXXX sympathizers.

propositions.text: Government takes maximalist approach in purges, targeting those with affinity or membership, not just coup participants.
propositions.quote: The NDP states that the government is a taking a maximalist position in purges, by going after those who have simply an affinity with or membership of the XXXX network, rather than going after those who actually participated in the coup.

paragraphs.summary: Reports show Turkish government rhetoric and actions aim to purge all XXXX supporters, including diaspora, with broad targeting beyond coup participants.

propositions.text: Council of Europe reports emergency decrees have wide scope, vague criteria, and weak evidence for sanctions.
propositions.quote: The Council of Europe (CE) states that the government's emergency decree-laws had an extremely wide scope of application, the use of vague terms such as "contacts", "relations" or "connections" and the way they were being implemented.

propositions.text: Serious sanctions like dismissals and arrests decided on weak or no evidence; denunciation can lead to prison.
propositions.quote: The report also noted the serious administrative sanctions with a permanent character, such as dismissals, arrests and detention measures that seem to be decided upon weak or in some cases seemingly non-existent evidence and vague criteria, such that simple denunciation might lead to someone being sent to prison.

propositions.text: Authorities use undisclosed list of 16 criteria to identify suspected XXXX connections.
propositions.quote: There is also an undisclosed list of 16 criteria used by authorities to identify those suspected of having connections, relations and contacts with "XXXX".

paragraphs.summary: Council of Europe reports emergency decrees use vague criteria and weak evidence for serious sanctions, with undisclosed criteria to identify XXXX suspects.

propositions.text: Decree on July 20, 2016 closed military schools and discharged staff, registering students elsewhere.
propositions.quote: The documentary evidence indicates that XXXX XXXX XXXX introduced on XXXX XXXX, 2016, made major changes to the army, announcing the discharge of military staff and the shutdown of all military schools, academies and non-commissioned officer training institutes. The decree also stated that students who continued their studies in war schools, faculty and colleges will be registered to appropriate faculties and colleges.

propositions.text: At least 4,000 students affected; government believes 95% of cadets identify with XXXX.
propositions.quote: On August 3, 2016 it was reported that at least 4,000 students were affected by the decree to close all military high schools and military academies and that the schools were closed because the government believes that they have been infiltrated by XXXX and that about 95% of the student body identifies with XXXX.

propositions.text: The Appellant is one such person affected by the decree.
propositions.quote: The Appellant is one such person affected.

paragraphs.summary: Decree closed military schools affecting 4,000 students, believing 95% are XXXX; the Appellant is among those affected.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence shows Turkish state arrests and detains soldiers and cadets, with continuing interest in similarly-situated persons.
propositions.quote: The documentary evidence in the record from the Appellant shows that the Turkish state has arrested and detained soldiers and cadets, and that there is a continuing interest of the Turkish state in persons similarly-situated to the Appellant.

propositions.text: Evidence includes arrests, detentions, probation, and dismissals of military personnel beyond those involved in coup.
propositions.quote: This includes cadets being arrested, detained and placed on probation, and evidence that the government dismissed 22,920 military personnel despite the fact that only 8,651 personnel, including cadets and conscripts, took part in the coup attempt.

propositions.text: Appellant testified about fellow cadets dismissed, detained, and arrested due to perceived coup involvement.
propositions.quote: In addition to the Appellant's own credible testimony about fellow cadets he knows who have been dismissed, detained and arrested due to their perceived involvement in the attempted coup,

propositions.text: Appellant submitted new evidence showing government continues arrests and detentions of military personnel including cadets.
propositions.quote: the Appellant submitted documentation as new evidence illustrating that the government is not done arresting and detaining military personnel, including cadets.

paragraphs.summary: Evidence shows Turkish state arrests and detains military personnel beyond coup participants; Appellant testified and submitted new evidence of ongoing arrests.

propositions.text: The Appellant provided his armed forces card and diploma identifying him as a person of concern to Turkish authorities for attending a closed military academy.
propositions.quote: the Appellant has provided his armed forces card and his diploma from XXXX University that refers to XXXX XXXX XXXX, which would identify him as a person of concern to Turkish authorities for having attended a military academy that was closed

propositions.text: Military academies were stated by the President to have 95% cadets as supporters of XXXX.
propositions.quote: Military academies that the President has stated 95% of the cadets were XXXX supporters

propositions.text: The Appellant has sought redress by bringing a case against the Turkish government but no outcome to date.
propositions.quote: The Appellant stated that he has sought redress by bringing a case against the Turkish government, but to date there has been no outcome

propositions.text: Given concerns about arbitrariness and lack of justice in Turkey post-coup, it is plausible the Appellant cannot clear his name.
propositions.quote: Given the concerns about the arbitrariness of the judicial process and lack of access to justice in Turkey following the attempted coup, it is plausible that the Appellant will be unable to clear his name

propositions.text: The Appellant's university degree designation has effectively blacklisted him as a perceived XXXX and member of XXXX.
propositions.quote: his university degree designated under XXXX XXXX has effectively blacklisted him as a perceived XXXX and member of XXXX

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Appellant's documents identify him as a person of concern, he sought redress without success, and is plausibly blacklisted in Turkey post-coup.

propositions.text: The Appellant provided documentary evidence showing lack of redress and socio-economic costs to those blacklisted for perceived XXXX support.
propositions.quote: The documentary evidence provided by the Appellant illustrates the lack of redress, as well as the ostracization and socio-economic cost to persons and family members who have been blacklisted for perceived support or affiliation with the XXXX XXXX

propositions.text: The Appellant's cousin, a military officer, was accused of XXXX affiliation, detained and tortured; his aunt was dismissed, detained, and released on probation.
propositions.quote: the Appellant provided evidence that his cousin, a military officer, was accused of being affiliated with the XXXX XXXX and was detained and tortured. His aunt was also dismissed from her job, detained and then released on probation

propositions.text: The court has no reason to doubt the Appellant's credibility on these facts.
propositions.quote: I have no reason to doubt the Appellant's credibility on this fact

propositions.text: The fear of arrest, dismissals, cancelled passports, employment difficulty, asset freezing, suspicion, stigma, and arbitrary detention amount to sustained human rights violations and well-founded fear of persecution.
propositions.quote: the constant fear of arrest for supporting the XXXX XXXX, the widespread dismissals, cancelled passports, difficulty obtaining new employment, the freezing of assets and the financial insecurity, the atmosphere of suspicion and the stigma attached to being a XXXX in today's Turkey, and the continuing arbitrariness to arrest and detention for actual or perceived involvement in the XXXX XXXX... amounts to a sustained violation of basic human rights and to a well-founded fear of persecution

paragraphs.summary: The court finds credible evidence of socio-economic harm and human rights violations against those perceived as XXXX supporters, causing well-founded fear of persecution.

propositions.text: The Appellant is undisputedly a XXXX XXXX, dismissed and transferred, with diploma designated as such under XXXX XXXX.
propositions.quote: Given the Appellant's undisputed identity as a XXXX XXXX, who was dismissed and transferred to another university, as well as his diploma being designated as such under XXXX XXXX

propositions.text: The Appellant is likely perceived as affiliated with the 'XXXX', also known as XXXX or XXXX XXXX.
propositions.quote: the evidence indicates that he is likely to be perceived as affiliated with the "XXXX", also known as the XXXX or XXXX XXXX

propositions.text: The Appellant has a profile subject to more than a mere possibility of persecution by the Turkish state forward-looking.
propositions.quote: I find the Appellant possesses a profile that is subject to more than a mere possibility of persecution by the Turkish state on a forward-looking basis

propositions.text: The Appellant has a nexus to the Convention as perceived political opinion or membership in a particular social group.
propositions.quote: The Appellant has a nexus to the Convention, being either perceived "political opinion" or perceived "membership in a particular social group"

propositions.text: There is no state protection or internal flight alternative as the state is the agent of harm everywhere in the country.
propositions.quote: there is no state protection or internal flight alternative for him as the state is the agent of harm and exists everywhere in the country

propositions.text: The RPD's finding about the Appellant's ability to exit Turkey without interest from authorities is not determinative; the test is forward-looking.
propositions.quote: in regard to the RPD's finding about the Appellant's ability to exit Turkey without being of interest to authorities, I find this is not determinative. The test is forward-looking

propositions.text: The Appellant is a Convention refugee.
propositions.quote: Therefore, I find the Appellant is a Convention refugee

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Appellant likely perceived as affiliated with XXXX, has a Convention nexus, no protection, and is a Convention refugee.

propositions.text: Pursuant to IRPA, the RAD sets aside the RPD's determination and finds the Appellant a Convention refugee with well-founded fear of persecution.
propositions.quote: Pursuant to paragraph 111(1)(b) of the IRPA, the RAD sets aside the determination of the RPD and substitutes its determination that the Appellant is a Convention refugee, as he has a well-founded fear of persecution

propositions.text: The appeal is allowed.
propositions.quote: This appeal is allowed

paragraphs.summary: The RAD sets aside the RPD decision, finds the Appellant a Convention refugee, and allows the appeal.
